mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months in at least 80% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.10 z-score) during episodes where GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates persistent supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.10 z-score) during periods of sustained industrial production contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and mortgage interest rates (RSAFS) over a three-month window signals an easing monetary and credit environment, which lowers borrowing costs and boosts corporate investment and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and RSAFS both decline for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 z-score) when both FEDFUNDS and RSAFS decline for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months signals a broad-based demand recovery, which raises earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both above 12-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 z-score) during episodes where both GDPC1 and HOUST exceed their 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer purchasing power and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.10 z-score) when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for six consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, which prompts central bank tightening and raises discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.10 z-score) during periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3% for six consecutive months.
